Following the ongoing 25% discount on AirPods Pro 3 and last week's $120 price drop on AirPods Max 2, 9to5Toys reported again this afternoon as a headline that Amazon has dropped AirTag 2 to a new all-time low, with the four-pack now at $80 (or $20 each). Additionally, the Apple M5 MacBook Pro with 24GB/1TB is down $320, while the 2TB M5 Pro sees an extra $500 off; also don't miss Anker's new SmartTrack "Find My" wallet card hitting a new Amazon all-time low at $25, as well as the LG 32-inch 6K Thunderbolt 5 monitor, a whopping $2,200 cheaper than the Apple Studio Display XDR (new all-time low). Read on for details.

The latest AirPods Pro 3 maintain their 25% discount, with the next generation widely expected to launch in 2027

  • AirPods Pro 3 $190 (original price $249)
  • AirPods Max 2 $429 (original price $549)
  • AirPods 4 $99 (original price $129)

Wow! AirTag 2 discounted again, four-pack hits new all-time low of $80 (or $20 each)

Great news! Amazon has just dropped the Apple 2026 AirTag 2 four-pack to a new all-time low, at just $20 per tracker.

Amazon is currently selling the AirTag 2 four-pack for $79.99, with free shipping.

Last week we were tracking the official pack at $89.99, then Amazon cut it to $85 yesterday, with a further reduction kicking off the new week. Priced at $99, that's roughly 20% off — doesn't sound like a lot, but it's a pretty significant discount for the latest AirTag 2.

On average, this pack works out to about $20 per AirTag, the lowest price since its launch earlier this year.

The single AirTag 2 listing remains at last week's Prime member free shipping low of $24, but the four-pack has dropped again to an even lower level.

Incidentally, the $20-per-tag price here matches the best open-box pricing we saw at Best Buy last week.

Apple 24GB/1TB M5 MacBook Pro down $320, 2TB M5 Pro down $500

Beyond the ongoing 25% discount on AirPods Pro 3 and the new low on AirTag 2, kicking off the new week we've also got a few notable MacBook Pro deals. Amazon still has the 2TB M5 Pro at $500 off, and we've also spotted a more affordable M5 MacBook Pro 24GB configuration down $300. Details below.

If you've had your eye on the more powerful M5 Pro, Amazon's $500-off model is definitely worth considering. But if a more affordable M5 better suits your needs, B&H's 14-inch 24GB/1TB configuration is also quite attractive:

B&H has again dropped the 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro with 24GB RAM and 1TB built-in storage to $1,899, with free shipping.

  • 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro 24GB/1TB $1,899 (original price $2,219)
  • Comes bundled with an upgraded 96W Apple charger

On this $2,199 machine, B&H also throws in the official 96W Apple charger — which costs an extra $20 to purchase from Apple's website.

Amazon currently sells the same MacBook Pro configuration for $2,049, but only with the standard 70W charger.

All told, B&H's deal saves you $320, matching the discount level mentioned earlier, and well below Amazon's current price.

However, as mentioned before, Amazon still has the 14-inch M5 Pro MacBook Pro 24GB/2TB at a significant discount, down to $2,699 — $500 below the $3,199 official MSRP — and this deal may not last long.

Anker's new SmartTrack "Find My" wallet card (supports iOS or Android) hits a new Amazon all-time low of $25

Anker recently launched the new SmartTrack "Find My" wallet card — the first product to support both Apple's tracking platform and Google Find Hub — now on sale at Amazon at a new all-time low of $25, with free shipping for Prime members.

The product only landed on Amazon last month at $35, dipped $5 by month's end, and now sees its first major discount, hitting a new Amazon all-time low.

The discount is nearly 30% off, matching the best deals we've seen on other wallet tracker cards this year.

I'm personally a huge fan of the Nomad tracking card — the standard version starts at $35, and the Pro version with 16-month battery life is $45 — but regardless of which you choose, I think everyone should put one in their wallet or cardholder. I never leave the house without mine.

Anker's latest SmartTrack Card E40 covers all the most important features, including wireless charging, and supports both Apple "Find My" and Google Find Hub platforms. At just 1.7mm thin, it has an alert volume of up to 80dB to help you locate it nearby — and of course you can also add it to the "Find My" and Find Hub apps to view its location on a map.

Tidy up your desk with this Anker smart power strip, now down to $58

LG 32-inch 6K Thunderbolt 5 monitor hits new low, a whopping $2,200 cheaper than Studio Display XDR

We just spotted a deal at B&H dropping the LG 32-inch UltraFine evo 6K monitor to $1,099.99, with free shipping. This monitor typically goes for $2,000, and has been hovering around $1,597 in recent weeks. Today's deal matches Amazon's all-time low earlier this month, and that price is still live. LG's own website also lists it at $1,100 today, so even if a particular retailer sells out, you've still got plenty of options. At this price, the UltraFine evo 6K is well below Apple's display offerings. The Studio Display XDR starts at $3,299, meaning the LG 32-inch 6K Thunderbolt 5 monitor is over $2,200 cheaper. Even the standard Studio Display starts at $1,549, so you'd save around $500 and get a larger 32-inch 6K screen. Read on for details.

The LG 32-inch UltraFine evo 6K is a high-end workstation monitor designed for creators, ideal for users who want a large, high-resolution screen but aren't looking to upgrade to Apple's pricier options. Its 6144 x 3456 screen packs over 21 million pixels at 224 PPI, giving plenty of room for editing timelines, full-resolution content, tools, and multiple windows. Color coverage reaches 99.5% Adobe RGB, and it supports VESA DisplayHDR 600 for better highlights and contrast. Connectivity is comprehensive too, including Thunderbolt 5, DisplayPort 2.1, HDMI, and USB-C. Mac users can also access calibrated color presets via LG's Studio Mode for more consistent creative output. Overall, this 6K monitor is feature-packed, suitable for anyone who wants truly expansive screen real estate without paying Apple's display prices.

If you don't want to spend over $1,000 on a new monitor, Woot also has deals on more affordable Samsung workstation monitors. The M series and other budget models are discounted, with entry prices as low as $118.

Today's accessory and charging deals:

  • This ultra-thin UGREEN wallet tracker card supports both iPhone and Android, now just $20 (new all-time low)
  • This compact UGREEN ultra-thin 45W Nexode Air charger is the slimmest in my EDC, now down to $27
  • Twelve South AirFly Pro wireless audio transmitter down to $40 at Amazon (black or white)
  • Chipolo Google Find Hub wallet card with action button/remote shutter, now $33
  • UGREEN MagFlow 25W Qi2.2 car charger back to $28 (original price $40)
  • Acer metal MagSafe golf cart phone mount down to $20, with free shipping for Prime members

The latest wireless Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro hits a new Amazon all-time low at nearly 30% off (wired version also available)

As part of a string of late-summer discounts on Fire tablets, Fire TV, and Blink smart home products, Amazon is offering the latest wireless Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro at its all-time low, and has repeated the Prime Day all-time low on the wired version — both at roughly 30% off retail.

  • Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro $180 (original price $250)
  • Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro $180 (original price $250)

Although Ring later released the more affordable Ring Peephole Cam 2K at $100, today we're focusing on a few particularly notable deals on its latest Pro series 4K models.

The Ring Wired Doorbell 4K Pro is now repeating the Prime Day all-time low, the first time we've seen this price since the late-June promotion. In fact, this is only the second time the model has dipped below $200.

The wireless Ring Battery Doorbell 4K Pro is now seeing its first discount, also at a new all-time low of $180.

As noted above, both models are priced at $250, or roughly 30% off — the best deals we've found and the lowest prices to date.

The two are largely similar, featuring retina 4K imaging, 10x enhanced zoom, night vision, and wide-angle views to clearly show you what's happening at your door; the wireless version includes the Quick Release Ultra battery pack for easy charging and simple installation (no wiring required), while the wired version offers "uninterrupted power, uninterrupted protection."

For more details, check out our product launch coverage from last September.

Best Buy launches new tech deals, NFL Sunday Ticket promotion, and preseason TV deals

Amazon drops $120 off AirPods Max 2 in all five colors (one of the best prices ever)

This week's big 60th anniversary sale brings one of the best prices ever for the Apple 2026 AirPods Max 2, with Amazon taking $120 off across all five colors.

Amazon has now dropped the Apple AirPods Max 2 to $429, with free shipping.

That's $120 off compared to the previous generation, also priced at $549 — the best price on a brand-new unit from a reputable retailer.

Best Buy has the Midnight Black version down to $403.99 with free shipping, in "excellent" open-box condition. While the price is lower, given the small difference, giving up a brand-new unit probably isn't worth it.

Apple released a true next-generation AirPods Max this year, unlike the previous generation which only changed colors and added a USB-C port. Unlike the in-ear AirPods lineup, its over-ear line won't be refreshed at next month's new product event, so this week you might consider grabbing these at $120 off — what could become Apple's premium over-ear headphones.

Only one previous promotion was cheaper than this — an earlier Prime Day this year, which was $30 below today's deal price — but stock was very unstable during that 4-day promotion.

Amazon launches this 512GB iPad mini at a new low, $450 off (Renewed Premium)

While iPad Air deals have only just started appearing this week, iPad discounts overall have been weak lately, or even nearly nonexistent. However, we've just spotted Amazon selling the 512GB iPad mini at a new low, with a massive $450 discount in top-tier Renewed Premium condition.

Amazon has now dropped the 512GB iPad mini A17 — the latest model — to $449, with free shipping.

That means this Apple-priced $899 iPad can now be purchased directly from Amazon at $450 off.

Worth noting: even before the price increase, we'd never seen this model brand-new below $679 at Amazon.

A reminder: Amazon's Renewed Premium models differ from regular Renewed products, as well as "excellent" condition refurbished units. Here's their standard:

  • Screen: If equipped with a screen, absolutely no scratches allowed.
  • Body: No visible cosmetic damage (scratches, dents, etc.) when viewed from 12 inches away.
  • Battery: If equipped, battery capacity exceeds 90% of original battery life.
  • Accessories: Comes with original or generic accessories and packaging.
  • Guarantee: Renewed Premium products come with a 365-day return policy.

Amazon's top-tier Premium Renewed iPhone 17 Pro now down $220 (matching Prime Day deals)

While Apple's official certified refurbished store is my first choice for iPhone deals, Apple hasn't yet listed the latest iPhone 17 Pro models there — looks like we'll have to wait until after the 18 series launches next month. Amazon's top-tier Premium Renewed stock has now been repriced to Prime Day levels, with brand-new unit discounts of up to $220.

To date, Amazon's top-tier Premium Renewed models are the most cost-effective way to get an unlocked iPhone 17 Pro. Not only do you save hundreds of dollars, but you also get a 1-year Amazon Renewed warranty and "over 90% original battery life" — rather than the 90-day warranty and incomparable battery life standards of non-Premium Renewed and Refurbished products.

Now the 1TB and 512GB iPhone 17 Pro models are again down by up to $220 — the 512GB version is $20 lower than the previously mentioned price:

  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,279 (original brand-new price $1,499)
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,279 (original brand-new price $1,499)
  • 1TB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,279 (original brand-new price $1,499)
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Cosmic Orange $1,179 (original brand-new price $1,299)
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Deep Blue $1,179 (original brand-new price $1,299)
  • 512GB iPhone 17 Pro Silver $1,179 (original brand-new price $1,299)

As highlighted in yesterday's Apple refurbished store feature, you can get a fully-featured iPhone 16 with 1-year Apple warranty starting from $699, or a 1TB 16 Pro Max for $1,269 — $330 cheaper than the corresponding 17 Pro Max, and $130 cheaper than the 512GB 17 Pro.

  • Refurbished iPhone 16 starting from $699 (up to $330 cheaper than the 17 series)
